Attributing the name of the cause to the effect in ﴿and do not consume﴾ and the like, since seizing is a cause of consuming. Naming a thing by what it was previously called, in ﴿and give the orphans﴾ [an-Nisa': 2], where He called them orphans after reaching maturity. Emphasis by following (ta'kīd bil-itbā') in ﴿wholesome and pleasant﴾ [an-Nisa': 4]. Naming a thing by what it will become, in ﴿a share of what he left﴾ [an-Nisa': 7], and in ﴿fire﴾ according to those who claim it is literal. Paronomasia (tajnīs): the identical kind in ﴿hand over﴾ and ﴿when you hand over﴾, and the different kind in ﴿and speak to them a fair word﴾ [an-Nisa': 8]. The addition of an element for an increase in meaning in ﴿let him be chaste﴾ [an-Nisa': 6]. Using the general for the particular in ﴿the relatives﴾, since what is meant is the holders of the prescribed shares. Using a place-adverb in place of a time-adverb in ﴿after them﴾, meaning after their death. Specification (ikhtiṣāṣ) in ﴿their bellies﴾, singling them out over others since they are the place of foods. Allusion (ta'rīḍ) in ﴿into their bellies﴾: he alluded by mentioning the bellies to their baseness and the lowering of their aspirations, and the Arabs disparage this, as the poet said:

"Leave noble deeds, do not travel in pursuit of them; sit, for you are the one who eats and dresses."

Emphasis of the literal sense by what removes the possibility of the figurative, by His saying ﴿into their bellies﴾. This removes the incidental figurative sense in His saying ﴿Would any of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother?﴾ [al-Hujurat: 12]. This is according to those who understood it literally; for those who understood it figuratively, it is in their view a supporting element of the figurative (tarshīḥ al-majāz). Similar to its removing the figurative is His saying ﴿flies with its two wings﴾ [al-An'am: 38], and His saying ﴿they write the Book with their own hands﴾ [al-Baqarah: 79]. Ellipsis (ḥadhf) occurs in many places, as in ﴿Allah instructs you concerning your children: for the male, a portion equal to that of two females﴾ [an-Nisa': 11]. When He left vague in His saying ﴿a share of what the parents and the relatives leave﴾ [an-Nisa': 7] the amounts and the relatives, He clarified in this verse the amounts and who among the relatives inherits. He began with the children and their inheritance from their parents, just as He began in His saying ﴿For men there is a share of what the parents leave﴾ [an-Nisa': 7] with them. In His saying ﴿Allah instructs you concerning your children﴾ [an-Nisa': 11] there is also a general statement which He clarified afterwards. He began with His saying "for the male," and what indicates His favor to them became clear. Mentioning the male first is more indicative of his favor than mentioning the explanation of the female's deficiency relative to him. Also, they used to give inheritance to males and not to females, so it sufficed for them that the female's share was doubled so that they would not be deprived, since they are connected through the bond of parenthood through which they are related.

The statements have differed concerning the occasion of revelation. The content of most of these sayings is that they did not give daughters any inheritance, as mentioned before, so this was revealed to clarify that and other matters. It was said: it was revealed concerning Jabir, when he fell ill, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ visited him, and he said: "How should I deal with my property?" It was also said: the inheritance was for the child and the bequest was for the parents, but this was abrogated by these verses (naskh). It was said: the meaning of ﴿instructs you﴾ (yūṣīkum) is "commands you." Like His saying ﴿That is what He has enjoined upon you﴾ [al-An'am: 151]. He turned to the word "instructs" because it is more eloquent and more indicative of concern and of seeking its quick realization. It was said: it means "charges you." Like His saying ﴿what He enjoined upon Noah﴾ [ash-Shura: 13]. It was said: it means "explains to you" the amounts concerning your children, which He established for them as a right absolutely by His saying "for the males," and ﴿those of the womb﴾ [al-Anfal: 75]. It was said: it means "prescribes for you." These are closely related statements.

The address in ﴿instructs you﴾ is to the believers. In ﴿your children﴾ there is an omitted modifier: "concerning the children of your deceased," because it is not permissible to address a living person about dividing the inheritance among his children and make that obligatory upon him. If the meaning of ﴿instructs you﴾ is "explains," then it is permissible to address the living person without needing to omit a modifier. The word "children" includes males and females, except that whoever has an impediment to inheritance is excluded from this generality. As for slavery, it is an impediment by consensus (ijma'). Disbelief is likewise, except for what Mu'adh held, that a Muslim inherits from a disbeliever. As for killing: if one kills his father, he does not inherit; likewise if he kills his grandfather, his brother, or his paternal uncle, he does not inherit from the blood money. This is the view of Ibn al-Musayyab, 'Ata', Mujahid, al-Zuhri, al-Awza'i, Malik, Ishaq, Abu Thawr, and Ibn al-Mundhir. Abu Hanifah, Sufyan, the people of opinion, al-Shafi'i, and Ahmad said: he does not inherit anything from the property nor from the blood money. Al-Nakha'i excepted from the generality of "your children" the captive, and said: he does not inherit.

The majority said: if his being alive is known, he inherits; if it is unknown, his ruling is the ruling of the missing person (mafqud). Inheritance from the Prophet ﷺ is excluded from the generality. As for the fetus: if it comes out dead, it does not inherit; if it comes out alive, al-Qasim, Ibn Sirin, al-Suddi, al-Sha'bi, al-Zuhri, Malik, and al-Shafi'i said: it must cry out loudly (yastahill ṣārikhan). Even if it sneezes, moves, cries out, suckles, or has breath in it. Al-Awza'i, Sufyan, and al-Shafi'i said: if its life is known by any of these, and even if it does not cry out, its ruling is the ruling of the living in inheritance. As for the fetus in its mother's womb, there is no disagreement that it inherits; the disagreement is only about the division of the property in which it has a share. That is mentioned in the books of jurisprudence. As for the hermaphrodite (khuntha), it is included in the generality of "your children," and there is no disagreement about giving it inheritance; the disagreement concerns what it inherits and by what it is known to be a hermaphrodite, and that is mentioned in the books of jurisprudence. As for the missing person, Abu Hanifah said: he does not inherit anything from anyone during his absence.

Al-Shafi'i said: his share is withheld until his death is verified, and this is the apparent view of Malik. As for the insane, the imbecile, and the feeble-minded (safih), they inherit by consensus. The word "child" is literally applied to the child of the loins, and it is used for the son's child, and the apparent view is that this is figurative. For if it were literal, by way of homonymy or common usage, it would apply to the child of the loins absolutely, and the ruling is that he does not inherit except when there is no child of the loins, or when there is someone present who does not take the whole inheritance from them.

This investigation also applies to the father, the grandfather, the mother, and the grandmother, and the more apparent view is that it is not in the literal sense, because the Companions agreed that the grandfather has no ruling mentioned in the Qur'an; if the name "father" applied to him literally, this consensus would not be valid. If someone bequeaths to "the child of so-and-so," then according to al-Shafi'i the child's child does not enter; according to Malik it enters; and according to Abu Hanifah it enters if so-and-so has no child of the loins.

Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 4, verse 11 (part 1 of 3):

And (lil-dhakari, "for the male"): either a noun is understood to be omitted, meaning "for the male among them," or the alif and lam (al-) substitute for the pronoun, according to the view of those who hold this estimation, "for their male." And (mithlu, "like"): an adjective of an omitted subject (mubtada'), whose estimated form is "a share like" (haẓḥun mithlu).

Al-Farra' said: "The verb yuwṣīkum ("He enjoins upon you") did not operate on (mithlu) because it is treated as the verb "say" in the reporting of sentences, so the sentence occupies a position of accusative (naṣb) governed by yuwṣīkum." Al-Kisa'i said: "(mithlu) is in the nominative case through the deletion of (an, "that"), its estimated form being: an lil-dhakari (that for the male)." Ibn Abi 'Ablah also read it this way. By His saying ﴿for the male is the like of the share of two females﴾ is meant the state in which the male and the two females are together: he has two shares, just as they have two shares. As for when a son stands alone, he takes the whole property, or when two daughters stand alone, the ruling on that will come later. The verse does not address the explicit ruling on these two cases.

Abu Muslim al-Isfahani said: "The share of the male here is two-thirds, so it must be that the share of the two females is [the same]." Abu Bakr al-Razi said: "If her share together with a male is a third, then her share together with a female being a third is more fitting, because the male is stronger than the female." It has been said: "The share of the two females is greater than the share of one female, for otherwise the male's share would equal the female's share, which contradicts the text. So their share must be two-thirds, since no one distinguishes between them." These are three considerations derived from the verse indicating that the obligatory share of two daughters is two-thirds. There is a fourth, based on clear analogy: the verse did not mention here the ruling for two females, but mentioned the ruling for one female and for what exceeds two. At the end of the surah it mentioned the ruling for one sister and the ruling for two sisters, but did not mention the ruling for more than two sisters. Thus the two verses are general in one respect and specified in another.

So we say: since the share of two sisters is two-thirds, two daughters are more entitled to it, because they are closer to the deceased. And since the share of many daughters does not exceed two-thirds, the share of sisters must likewise not exceed that, because the daughter, being more closely connected to the deceased, makes it impermissible to give the weaker a share greater than the stronger.

Al-Maturidi said: "The verse is evidence that the whole property belongs to the male when there is no female with him, because He gave the male the like of what is given to the two females. He has given the female half when no male is with her, by His saying ﴿and if she is one, then for her is half﴾. This indicates that the male, when alone, has twice that, and twice half is the whole." End of quotation.

Al-Hasan and Ibn Abi 'Ablah read (yuwaṣṣīkum) with doubled sad (tashdid). Al-Hasan, Nu'aym ibn Maysara and al-A'raj read thuluthan, wal-thuluth, wal-rub', wal-sudus, wal-thumun with the middle letter sukun (sukūn al-wasṭ), whereas the majority read them with ḍamma. This is the dialect of the Hijaz and Banu Asad, as reported by al-Nahhas, from thuluth to 'ushr. Al-Zajjaj said: "It is one dialect, and the sukun is a lightening." The estimated meaning of the verse is: "Allah enjoins upon you concerning your children, who are heirs, that for the male among them is a share like the share of two females, in the state of their being together, from what the testators have left, if the child inherits alone. If there is with them one who has a fixed share (dhu farḍ), then what remains of the property is for them. The fixed shares are those mentioned in the Qur'an, and they are six: the half, the quarter, the eighth, the two-thirds, the third, and the sixth."

﴿If they are women above two, then for them is two-thirds of what he left.﴾ The apparent sense of this division is that what exceeds two of the children inherit two-thirds of what their deceased parent left, and the apparent context restricts the heirs to them. Since the word "children" includes males and females, and here the intent is to state the ruling for females, the pronoun is made exclusively feminine. The females are one of the two categories to which the word "children" applies, so the pronoun returns to one of the two categories. It is as if His saying ﴿concerning your children﴾ were equivalent to ﴿concerning your children, males and females﴾. If the pronoun may return to a rational masculine broken plural with the ending of the sound masculine plural, as in His saying "the lord of the devils and those whom they misled" (wa-rabba al-shayāṭīn wa-man aḍlalna), and as it returns to females, as in His saying ﴿and the mothers suckle﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:233], then it is more fitting that it return to a rational broken plural that includes both masculine and feminine, by considering the one of the two categories that is feminine. The subject of (kāna, "was") is the pronoun returning to one of the two categories of children, and the predicate is (nisā'an, "women") with its qualifier, which is "above two," because the predicate's meaning is not complete with "women" alone. The qualifier serves to emphasize and removes the possibility that the plural before them is meant metaphorically, since a plural may be used to express comparison. Al-Zamakhshari permitted (nisā'an) as a second predicate of (kāna), but this is not correct, because a predicate must itself complete the meaning of the predication. If one stopped at His saying ﴿If they are women﴾, it would be like saying "if the Zayds were men," which is not a complete sentence.

Some Basran grammarians said: the estimate is "and if the ones left behind were women above two." Al-Zamakhshari estimated it as: "the daughters or the female children."

Al-Zamakhshari said: "If you ask, can the pronouns in (kunna, "they were") and (kānat, "she was") be indefinite, with (nisā'an) and (wāḥidatan) as their explanation, on the basis that (kāna) is a complete verb? I say: I do not rule that out." End of quotation. By "indefinite" we mean that they do not refer back to an earlier explained referent, but their explanation is the accusative noun that follows them. What al-Zamakhshari did not rule out is distant, or entirely impermissible, because (kāna) is not among the verbs whose subject is a pronoun explained by what follows it. Rather, among verbs it is specific to ni'ma and bi'sa and what is analogized to them, and to the matter of contention (tanāzu') as established in grammar.

The meaning of ﴿above two﴾ is: more than two, whatever number they reach, so for them there is only two-thirds. Whoever claims that the meaning of His saying ﴿women above two﴾ is two or more, and that the force of the statement requires this, as Ibn 'Atiyyah did, or that (fawq, "above") is superfluous, citing that (fawq) is used superfluously in His saying ﴿strike above the necks﴾ [al-Anfal 8:12], needs no proof to refute his claim, because its error is clear. They mention that the ruling for two females in inheritance is two-thirds, like daughters. They say: no one disagreed on this except Ibn 'Abbas, who holds that the two of them have half when alone, just as their state when together with a male, and what they argued with has already been mentioned. It is reported in the hadith concerning the case of Aws ibn Thabit that "he gave the two daughters two-thirds." The daughters of a son, or full sisters, or consanguine sisters, are like the daughters of the back (ṣulb) in receiving two-thirds when they stand alone without someone who excludes them.

﴿And if she is one, then for her is half.﴾ The majority read (wāḥidatan) with fatḥa, as the predicate of (kāna), meaning: if she, that is the daughter, is alone with no other with her. Nafi' read (wāḥidatun) with ḍamma, treating (kāna) as complete and (wāḥidatun) as its subject. As-Sulami read (al-nuṣf) with ḍamma on the nun, which is the reading of 'Ali and Zayd throughout the Qur'an. The disagreement over ḍamma and kasra on the nun in His saying ﴿so half of what you have fixed﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:237] has already been discussed in al-Baqarah. The daughter of a son, when there is no daughter of the back with her, the full sister or consanguine sister, and the husband when the wife has no child, nor a son's child, are like the daughter of the back: each of them has half.

﴿And for his parents, to each one of them is a sixth of what he left, if he has a child.﴾ When He mentioned the descendants and the amount they inherit, He began mentioning the ascendants and the amount they inherit. He stated that the deceased's parents inherit, each one, a sixth, if the deceased has a child. His parents are his father and his mother. The word "father" was used in the dual, as it is said "al-qamarān" (the two moons), where "the moon" predominates over "the sun" because of its masculine gender; this dual is not analogized. His saying "if he has a child" covers male and female, singular and plural.

The apparent sense of the verse is that the father's fixed share is a sixth if the deceased has a child, whatever child it is, (p-183) and the remainder of the property goes to the child, whether male or female. According to the majority, if the child is female, the father takes the sixth as a fixed share and the rest as residue (ta'ṣīb). The Rawafiḍ clung to the apparent wording of "child" and said: a sixth for each of the two parents, and the rest for the daughter or son, since "child" applies to the male, the female, the grandfather, the daughters of a son together with a daughter, the consanguine sisters together with a full sister, a single one of the maternal siblings, and the grandmothers, like the father with a daughter for the sixth. Malik said: the grandmother of the father's father does not inherit. Ibn Sirin said: the mother's mother does not inherit.

The pronoun in (li-abawayhi, "for his parents") refers back to what the pronoun in (taraka, "he left") refers to, which is the pronoun of the deceased, indicated by the meaning and context of the speech. ﴿To each one of them﴾ is a substitution (badal) for (abawayhi), and conveys the sense of detail and clarifies that the sixth belongs to each one, since without this substitution the apparent sense would be that they share the sixth, and this is more eloquent and emphatic than saying "for each one of his parents is a sixth," since their mention is repeated twice: once explicitly and once by the pronoun referring to them. Al-Zamakhshari said: "(al-sudus) is the subject (mubtada'), and its predicate is (li-abawayhi), and the substitution lies between them." End of quotation. Abu al-Baqa' said: "(al-sudus) is nominative by beginning (ibtida'), and ﴿to each one of them﴾ is the predicate, (li-kull) is a substitution from (al-abawayn), and (minhuma) is an adjective of (wāḥid)." This substitution is a substitution of part from whole, which is why the pronoun is used, and it is not to be supposed that it is a substitution of one thing for another, since they are the same referent, because one may say "your parents do such-and-such," but not "your parents, each one of them, do such-and-such"; rather you say "does such-and-such." In al-Zamakhshari's statement, "(al-sudus) is the subject and its predicate is (li-abawayhi)," there is an issue: the substitution is what has the predicate, not the substituted element, as we illustrated in your saying "your parents, each one of them, does such-and-such," when we parse kull as a substitution. Just as you say "indeed Zayd, his eye is beautiful," so when the substitution is a predicate, the substituted element is not the predicate, and it is dispensed with: the substituted element is dispensed with the predicate of the substitution, just as the predicate of "inna" is dispensed with the substituted element, namely the subject of "inna," by reporting about the substitution. If the structure were "wa-li-abawayhi al-sudusān" (and for his parents are two sixths), it would give the impression of equal halving or preference in amount between the two parents; so this Qur'anic structure is most explicit and eloquent. The apparent sense of His saying ﴿for his parents﴾ is that they are the two who begot the deceased directly, not his grandfathers or any ancestors above them. They claimed that His saying "your children" includes descendants of lower generations; they said: because "parents" is a dual word that does not admit generality or plurality, unlike His saying "among your children." In this there is consideration. In my view the two are equal in signification: if the word is taken in its literal sense, it covers only the children whom the two parents directly begot, and not those lower, just as "parents" covers only the two who directly begot him, not those above. Or if the word is taken in its figurative sense, then the two words share this meaning, so "parents" applies to those who directly begot him and to ancestors above him, just as "children" applies to those whom he directly begot and to those below him. And the descendants (those lower) show, in both places, that the literal sense is intended: a son's son does not inherit in place of the son, and the grandmother is not assigned the third by consensus, so the son's son is not given the status of the son in his presence, nor the grandmother the status of the mother.

* *

فَإنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ ولَدٌ ووَرِثَهُ أبَواهُ فَلِأُمِّهِ الثُّلُثُ ﴿"If he has no child and his parents are his heirs, then his mother receives a third."﴾ قَوْلُهُ: ﴿فَإنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ ولَدٌ﴾ قَسِيمٌ لِقَوْلِهِ: ﴿إنْ كانَ لَهُ ولَدٌ﴾ (the complementary case, *qasim*, i.e., the other half of a division of cases), و﴿ورِثَهُ أبَواهُ﴾ دَلِيلٌ عَلى أنَّهُما انْفَرَدا بِمِيراثِهِ، لَيْسَ مَعَهُما أحَدٌ مِن أهْلِ السِّهامِ (those entitled to fixed shares, *ahl al-sihham*)، لا ولَدٌ ولا غَيْرُهُ، فَيَكُونُ قَوْلُهُ: ﴿ووَرِثَهُ أبَواهُ﴾ حُكْمًا لَهُما بِجَمِيعِ المالِ. فَإذا خَلُصَ لِلْأُمِّ الثُّلُثُ كانَ الثّانِي وهو الثُّلُثانِ لِلْأبِ، فَذِكْرُ القِسْمِ الواحِدِ يَدُلُّ عَلى الآخَرِ؛ كَما تَقُولُ: هَذا المالُ لِزَيْدٍ وعَمْرٍو، لِزَيْدٍ مِنهُ الثُّلُثُ، فَيُعْلَمُ قَطْعًا أنَّ باقِيَهُ وهو الثُّلُثانِ لِعَمْرٍو. فَلَوْ كانَ مَعَهُما زَوْجٌ كانَ لِلْأُمِّ السُّدُسُ، وهو الثُّلُثُ بِالإضافَةِ إلى الأبِ. وقالَ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ وشُرَيْحٌ: لِلْأُمِّ الثُّلُثُ مِن جَمِيعِ المالِ مَعَ الزَّوْجِ، والنِّصْفُ لِلزَّوْجِ، وما بَقِيَ لِلْأبِ، فَيَكُونُ مَعْنى: ﴿ووَرِثَهُ أبَواهُ﴾ مُنْفَرِدَيْنِ، أوْ مَعَ غَيْرِ ولَدٍ، وهَذا مُخالِفٌ لِظاهِرِ قَوْلِهِ: ﴿ووَرِثَهُ أبَواهُ﴾. إذْ يَدُلُّ عَلى أنَّهُما انْفَرَدا بِالإرْثِ، فَيَتَقاسَمانِ: لِلذَّكَرِ مِثْلُ حَظِّ الأُنْثَيَيْنِ. ولا شَكَّ أنَّ الأبَ أقْوى في الإرْثِ مِنَ الأُمِّ، إذْ يَضْعُفُ نَصِيبُهُ عَلى نَصِيبِها إذا انْفَرَدا بِالإرْثِ، ويَرِثُ بِالفَرْضِ (fixed share, *fard*) وبِالتَّعْصِيبِ (residuary inheritance, *ta'sib*) وبِهِما. وفي قَوْلِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ وشُرَيْحٍ: يَكُونُ لَها مَعَ الزَّوْجِ والأبِ مِثْلُ حَظِّ الذَّكَرَيْنِ، فَتَصِيرُ أقْوى مِنَ الأبِ، وتَصِيرُ الأُنْثى لَها مِثْلا حَظِّ الذَّكَرِ، ولا دَلِيلَ عَلى ذَلِكَ مِن نَصٍّ ولا قِياسٍ.

وفِي إقامَةِ الجَدِّ مَقامَ الأبِ خِلافٌ. فَمَن قالَ: أنَّهُ أبٌ وحَجَبَ بِهِ الإخْوَةَ - جَماعَةٌ، مِنهم: أبُو بَكْرٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ، ولَمْ يُخالِفْهُ أحَدٌ مِنَ الصَّحابَةِ في أيّامِ حَياتِهِ. وقالَ بِمَقالَتِهِ بَعْدَ وفاتِهِ: أُبَيٌّ، ومُعاذٌ، وأبُو الدَّرْداءِ، وابْنُ عَبّاسٍ، وابْنُ الزُّبَيْرِ، والأعْمَشُ، وعائِشَةُ، وعَطاءٌ، وطاوُسُ، والحَسَنُ، والسُّدِّيُّ، وأبُو حَنِيفَةَ، وإسْحاقُ، وأبُو ثَوْرٍ. وذَهَبَ عَلِيٌّ، وزَيْدٌ، وابْنُ مَسْعُودٍ: إلى تَوْرِيثِ الجَدِّ مَعَ الإخْوَةِ، ولا يُنْقَصُ مِنَ الثُّلُثِ مَعَ الإخْوَةِ لِلْأبِ والأُمِّ أوْ لِلْأُمِّ أوْ لِلْأبِ، إلّا مَعَ ذَوِي الفُرُوضِ، فَإنَّهُ لا يُنْقَصُ مَعَهم مِنَ السُّدُسِ شَيْئًا في قَوْلِ زَيْدٍ، وهو قَوْلُ: مالِكٍ، والأوْزاعِيِّ، والشّافِعِيِّ، ومُحَمَّدٍ، وأبِي يُوسُفَ. وكانَ عَلِيٌّ يُشْرِكُ بَيْنَ الجَدِّ والإخْوَةِ في السُّدُسِ، ولا يُنْقِصُهُ مِنَ السُّدُسِ شَيْئًا مَعَ ذَوِي الفُرُوضِ وغَيْرِهِمْ، وهو قَوْلُ ابْنِ أبِي لَيْلى. وذَهَبَ الجُمْهُورُ: إلى أنَّ الجَدَّ يُسْقِطُ بَنِي الإخْوَةِ مِنَ المِيراثِ، إلّا ما رُوِيَ عَنِ الشَّعْبِيِّ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ: أنَّهُ أجْرى بَنِي الإخْوَةِ في المُقاسَمَةِ مَجْرى الإخْوَةِ.

وأمّا أُمُّ الأُمِّ فَتُسَمّى أُمًّا مَجازًا، لَكِنْ لا يُفْرَضُ لَها الثُّلُثُ إجْماعًا (consensus, *ijma'*)، وأجْمَعُوا عَلى أنَّ لِلْجَدَّةِ السُّدُسَ إذا لَمْ يَكُنْ لِلْمَيِّتِ أُمٌّ، وعَلى أنَّ الأُمَّ تَحْجُبُ أُمَّها وأُمَّ الأبِ، وعَلى أنَّ الأبَ لا يَحْجُبُ أُمَّ الأُمِّ. واخْتَلَفُوا في تَوْرِيثِ الجَدَّةِ وابْنَتِها. فَرُوِيَ عَنْ عُثْمانَ وعَلِيٍّ وزَيْدٍ: أنَّها لا تَرِثُ وابْنَتُها حَيَّةٌ، وبِهِ قالَ الأوْزاعِيُّ، والثَّوْرِيُّ، ومالِكٌ، وأبُو ثَوْرٍ، وأصْحابُ الرَّأْيِ. ورُوِيَ عَنْ عُثْمانَ وعَلِيٍّ أيْضًا، وعُمَرَ وابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ وأبِي مُوسى وجابِرٍ: أنَّها تَرِثُ مَعَها. وقالَ بِهِ شُرَيْكٌ، وعُبَيْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ الحَسَنِ، وأحْمَدُ، وإسْحاقُ، وابْنُ المُنْذِرِ. وقالَ: كَما أنَّ الجَدَّ لا يَحْجُبُهُ إلّا الأبُ، كَذَلِكَ الجَدَّةُ لا يَحْجُبُها إلّا الأُمُّ. وقَرَأ الأخَوانِ (حمزة والكسائي): ﴿فَلِإمِّهِ﴾ هُنا مَوْضِعَيْنِ، وفي القَصَصِ ﴿في إمِّها﴾ وفي الزُّخْرُفِ: في ﴿إمِّ الكِتابِ﴾ بِكَسْرِ الهَمْزَةِ، لِمُناسَبَةِ الكَسْرَةِ والياءِ. وكَذا قَرَأ ﴿مِن بُطُونِ إمَّهاتِكم﴾ في النَّحْلِ والزَّمَرِ والنَّجْمِ، ﴿أوْ بُيُوتِ إمَّهاتِكم﴾ في النُّورِ. وزادَ حَمْزَةُ في هَذِهِ كَسْرَ المِيمِ إتْباعًا لِكَسْرَةِ الهَمْزَةِ [p-185] وهَذا في الدَّرَجِ (in continuous recitation). فَإذا ابْتَدَأ يَضُمُّ الهَمْزَةَ، وهي قِراءَةُ الجَماعَةِ دَرَجًا وابْتِداءً. وذَكَرَ سِيبَوَيْهِ أنَّ كَسْرَ الهَمْزَةِ مِن أُمٍّ بَعْدَ الياءِ، والكَسْرُ لُغَةٌ. وذَكَرَ الكِسائِيُّ والفَرّاءُ: أنَّها لُغَةُ هَوازِنَ وهُذَيْلٍ.

﴿فَإنْ كانَ لَهُ إخْوَةٌ فَلِأُمِّهِ السُّدُسُ﴾ ﴿"But if he has siblings, then his mother receives a sixth."﴾ وصارَ الأبُ يَأْخُذُ خَمْسَةَ الأسْداسِ. وذَهَبَ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ إلى أنَّ الإخْوَةَ يَأْخُذُونَ ما حَجَبُوا الأُمَّ عَنْهُ وهو السُّدُسُ، ولا يَأْخُذُهُ الأبُ. ورُوِيَ عَنْهُ: أنَّ الأبَ يَأْخُذُهُ لا الإخْوَةَ، لِقَوْلِ الجَماعَةِ مِنَ العُلَماءِ. قالَ السُّدِّيُّ: وإنَّما أخَذَهُ الأبُ دُونَهم لِأنَّهُ يَمُونُهم ويَلِي نِكاحَهم والنَّفَقَةَ عَلَيْهِمْ. وظاهِرُ لَفْظِ (إخْوَةٌ) اخْتِصاصُهُ بِالجَمْعِ المُذَكَّرِ؛ لِأنَّ (إخْوَةٌ) جَمْعُ أخٍ. وقَدْ ذَهَبَ إلى ذَلِكَ طائِفَةٌ، فَقالُوا: الإخْوَةُ تَحْجُبُ الأُمَّ عَنِ الثُّلُثِ دُونَ الأخَواتِ، وعِنْدَنا يَتَناوَلُ الجَمْعَيْنِ عَلى سَبِيلِ التَّغْلِيبِ. فَإذَنْ يَصِيرُ المُرادُ بِقَوْلِهِ: (إخْوَةٌ) مُطْلَقَ الأُخُوَّةِ، أيْ: أشِقّاءُ، أوْ لِأبٍ، أوْ لِأُمٍّ، ذُكُورًا أوْ إناثًا، أوِ الصِّنْفَيْنِ. وظاهِرُ لَفْظِ (إخْوَةٌ) الجَمْعُ. وأنَّ الَّذِينَ يَحُطُّونَ الأُمَّ إلى السُّدُسِ ثَلاثَةٌ فَصاعِدًا، وهو قَوْلُ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ: الأخَواتُ عِنْدَهُ في حُكْمِ الواحِدِ لا يُحَطّانِ كَما لا يُحَطُّ، فالجُمْهُورُ عَلى أنَّ الأخَوَيْنِ حُكْمُهُما في الحَطِّ حُكْمُ الثَّلاثِ فَصاعِدًا.

ومَنشَأُ الخِلافِ: هَلِ الجَمْعُ أقَلُّهُ اثْنانِ أوْ ثَلاثَةٌ؟ وهي مَسْألَةٌ يُبْحَثُ فِيها في أُصُولِ الفِقْهِ، والبَحْثُ فِيها في عِلْمِ النَّحْوِ ألْيَقُ. وقالَ الزَّمَخْشَرِيُّ: الإخْوَةُ تُفِيدُ مَعْنى الجَمْعِيَّةِ المُطْلَقَةِ بِغَيْرِ كَمِّيَّةٍ، والتَّثْنِيَةُ كالتَّثْلِيثِ والتَّرْبِيعِ في إفادَةِ الكَمِّيَّةِ، وهو مَوْضِعُ الدَّلالَةِ عَلى الجَمْعِ المُطْلَقِ، فَدَلَّ بِالإخْوَةِ عَلَيْهِ، انْتَهى. ولا نُسَلِّمُ لَهُ دَعْوى أنَّ الإخْوَةَ تُفِيدُ مَعْنى الجَمْعِيَّةِ المُطْلَقَةِ، بَلْ تُفِيدُ مَعْنى الجَمْعِيَّةِ الَّتِي بَعْدَ التَّثْنِيَةِ بِغَيْرِ كَمِّيَّةٍ فِيما بَعْدَ التَّثْنِيَةِ، فَيَحْتاجُ في إثْباتِ دَعَواهُ إلى دَلِيلٍ. وظاهِرُ (إخْوَةٌ) الإطْلاقُ، فَيَتَناوَلُ الإخْوَةَ مِنَ الأُمِّ فَيَحْجُبُونَ كَما قُلْنا قَبْلُ. وذَهَبَ الرَّوافِضُ: إلى أنَّ الإخْوَةَ مِنَ الأُمِّ لا يَحْجُبُونَ الأُمَّ، لِأنَّهم يُدْلُونَ بِها، فَلا يَجُوزُ أنْ يَحْجُبُوها ويَجْعَلُوهُ لِغَيْرِها فَيَصِيرُونَ ضارِّينَ لَها نافِعِينَ لِغَيْرِها. واسْتُدِلَّ بِهَذِهِ الآيَةِ عَلى أنَّ البِنْتَ تَقْلِبُ حَقَّ الأُمِّ مِنَ الثُّلُثِ إلى السُّدُسِ بِقَوْلِهِ: ﴿فَإنْ كانَ لَهُ إخْوَةٌ﴾؛ لِأنَّها إذا حُرِمَتِ الثُّلُثَ بِالإخْوَةِ وانْتَقَلَتْ إلى السُّدُسِ فَلَأنْ تُحْرَمَ بِالبِنْتِ أوْلى.

﴿مِن بَعْدِ وصِيَّةٍ يُوصِي بِها أوْ دَيْنٍ﴾ ﴿"after any bequest he makes or debt."﴾ المَعْنى: أنَّ قِسْمَةَ المالِ بَيْنَ مَن ذُكِرَ إنَّما تَكُونُ بَعْدَ خُرُوجِ ما يَجِبُ إخْراجُهُ بِوَصِيَّةٍ، أوْ بِدَيْنٍ. ولَيْسَ تَعَلُّقُ الدَّيْنِ والوَصِيَّةِ بِالتَّرِكَةِ سَواءً، إذْ لَوْ هَلَكَ مِنَ التَّرِكَةِ شَيْءٌ قَبْلَ القِسْمَةِ ذَهَبَ مِنَ الوَرَثَةِ والمُوصى لَهُ جَمِيعًا، ويَبْقى الباقِي بَيْنَهم بِالشَّرِكَةِ، ولا يَسْقُطُ مِنَ الدَّيْنِ شَيْءٌ بِهَلاكِ شَيْءٍ مِنَ التَّرِكَةِ. وتَفْصِيلُ [p-186] المِيراثِ عَلى ما ذَكَرُوا أنَّهُ بَعْدَ الوَصِيَّةِ يَدُلُّ عَلى أنَّهُ لا يُرادُ ظاهِرُ إطْلاقِ وصِيَّةٍ مِن جَوازِ الوَصِيَّةِ بِقَلِيلِ المالِ وكَثِيرِهِ، بَلْ دَلَّ ذَلِكَ عَلى جَوازِ الوَصِيَّةِ بِنَقْصِ المالِ. ويُبَيِّنُ أيْضًا ذَلِكَ قَوْلُهُ: ﴿لِلرِّجالِ نَصِيبٌ﴾ [النساء: ٣٢] الآيَةَ. إذْ لَوْ جازَتِ الوَصِيَّةُ بِجَمِيعِ المالِ لَكانَ هَذا الجَوازُ ناسِخًا لِهَذِهِ الآيَةِ، وقَدْ دَلَّ الخَبَرُ الَّذِي تَلَقَّتْهُ الأُمَّةُ بِالقَبُولِ عَلى أنَّ الوَصِيَّةَ غَيْرُ جائِزَةٍ في أكْثَرَ مِنَ الثُّلُثِ. وقَدِ اسْتَحَبُّوا النُّقْصانَ عَنْهُ، هَذا إذا كانَ لَهُ وارِثٌ، فَإنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ وارِثٌ، فَقالَ مالِكٌ والأوْزاعِيُّ والحَسَنُ بْنُ صالِحٍ: لا تَجُوزُ الوَصِيَّةُ إلّا في الثُّلُثِ. وقالَ شَرِيكٌ وأبُو حَنِيفَةَ وأصْحابُهُ: يَجُوزُ بِجَمِيعِ مالِهِ؛ لِأنَّ الِامْتِناعَ في الوَصِيَّةِ بِأكْثَرَ مِنَ الثُّلُثِ مُعَلَّلٌ بِوُجُودِ الوَرَثَةِ، فَإذا لَمْ يُوجَدْ وأجازَ لِظاهِرِ إطْلاقِ الوَصِيَّةِ، لِأنَّهُ إذا فُقِدَ مُوجِبُ تَخْصِيصِ البَعْضِ جازَ حَمْلُ اللَّفْظِ عَلى ظاهِرِهِ.

وقَدِ اسْتُدِلَّ بِقَوْلِهِ: ﴿مِن بَعْدِ وصِيَّةٍ يُوصِي بِها أوْ دَيْنٍ﴾ عَلى أنَّهُ إذا لَمْ يَكُنْ دَيْنٌ لِآدَمِيٍّ ولا وصِيَّةٌ يَكُونُ جَمِيعُ مالِهِ لِوَرَثَتِهِ وأنَّهُ إنْ كانَ عَلَيْهِ حَجٌّ أوْ زَكاةٌ أوْ كَفّارَةٌ أوْ نَذْرٌ لا يَجِبُ إخْراجُهُ إلّا أنْ يُوصِيَ بِذَلِكَ. وفي هَذا الِاسْتِدْلالِ نَظَرٌ. والوَصِيَّةُ مَندُوبٌ إلَيْها، وقَدْ كانَتْ واجِبَةً قَبْلَ نُزُولِ الفَرائِضِ فَنُسِخَتْ. وادَّعى قَوْمٌ وُجُوبَها. وتَتَعَلَّقُ (مِن) بِمَحْذُوفٍ، أيْ: يَسْتَحِقُّونَ ذَلِكَ، كَما فَصَّلَ ﴿مِن بَعْدِ وصِيَّةٍ﴾، و﴿يُوصِي﴾ في مَوْضِعِ الصِّفَةِ، و(بِها) مُتَعَلِّقٌ بِـ﴿يُوصِي﴾، وهو مُضارِعٌ وقَعَ مَوْقِعَ الماضِي. والمَعْنى: مِن بَعْدِ وصِيَّةٍ أوْصى بِها. ومَعْنى: (أوْ دَيْنٍ) لَزِمَهُ. وقَدَّمَ الوَصِيَّةَ عَلى الدَّيْنِ، وإنْ كانَ أداءُ الدَّيْنِ هو المُقَدَّمَ عَلى الوَصِيَّةِ بِإجْماعٍ اهْتِمامًا بِها وبَعْثًا عَلى إخْراجِها، إذْ كانَتْ مَأْخُوذَةً مِن غَيْرِ عِوَضٍ شاقًّا عَلى الوَرَثَةِ إخْراجُها مَظِنَّةً لِلتَّفْرِيطِ فِيها، بِخِلافِ الدَّيْنِ. فَإنَّ نَفْسَ الوارِثِ مُوَطَّنَةٌ عَلى أدائِهِ، ولِذَلِكَ سَوّى بَيْنَها وبَيْنَ الدَّيْنِ بِلَفْظِ (أوْ) في الوُجُوبِ. أوْ لِأنَّ الوَصِيَّةَ مَندُوبٌ إلَيْها في الشَّرْعِ مَحْضُوضٌ عَلَيْها، فَصارَتْ لِلْمُؤْمِنِ كالأمْرِ اللّازِمِ لَهُ. والدَّيْنُ لا يَلْزَمُ أنْ يُوجَدَ، إذْ قَدْ يَكُونُ عَلى المَيِّتِ دَيْنٌ وقَدْ لا يَكُونُ، فَبُدِئَ بِما كانَ وُقُوعُهُ كاللّازِمِ، وأُخِّرَ ما لا يَلْزَمُ وُجُودُهُ. ولِهَذِهِ الحِكْمَةِ كانَ العَطْفُ بِـ(أوْ)، إذْ لَوْ كانَ الدَّيْنُ لا يَمُوتُ أحَدٌ إلّا وهو راتِبٌ لازِمٌ لَهُ، لَكانَ العَطْفُ بِالواوِ، أوْ لِأنَّ الوَصِيَّةَ حَظُّ مَساكِينَ وضِعافٍ، والدَّيْنَ حَظُّ غَرِيمٍ يَطْلُبُهُ بِقُوَّةٍ. ولَهُ فِيهِ مَقالٌ. قالَ الزَّمَخْشَرِيُّ: فَإنْ قُلْتَ: ما مَعْنى (أوْ)؟ قُلْتُ: مَعْناها الإباحَةُ، وأنَّهُ إنْ كانَ أحَدُهُما أوْ كِلاهُما قُدِّمَ عَلى قِسْمَةِ المِيراثِ كَقَوْلِكَ: جالِسِ الحَسَنَ أوِ ابْنِ سِيرِينَ. انْتَهى.

ودَلَّتِ الآيَةُ عَلى أنَّ المِيراثَ لا يَكُونُ إلّا بَعْدَ إخْراجِ ما وجَبَ بِالوَصِيَّةِ أوِ الدَّيْنِ، فَدَلَّ عَلى أنَّ إخْراجَ ما وجَبَ بِها سابِقٌ عَلى المِيراثِ، ولَمْ يَدُلَّ عَلى أنَّهُما أسْبَقُ ما يُخْرَجُ مِن مالِ المَيِّتِ، إذِ الأسْبَقُ هو مُؤْنَةُ تَجْهِيزِهِ مِن غُسْلِهِ وتَكْفِينِهِ وحَمْلِهِ ووَضْعِهِ في قَبْرِهِ، أوْ ما يُحْتاجُ إلَيْهِ مِن ذَلِكَ. وقَرَأ الِابْنانِ وأبُو بَكْرٍ: (يُوصى) فِيهِما مَبْنِيًّا لِلْمَفْعُولِ، وتابَعَهم حَفْصٌ عَلى الثّانِي فَقَطْ، وقَرَأهُما الباقُونَ مَبْنِيًّا لِلْفاعِلِ.

﴿آباؤُكم وأبْناؤُكم لا تَدْرُونَ أيُّهم أقْرَبُ لَكم نَفْعًا﴾ ﴿"Your fathers and your sons—you do not know which of them is closer to you in benefit."﴾ قالَ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ والحَسَنُ: هو في الآخِرَةِ، لا يَدْرُونَ أيُّ الوالِدَيْنِ أرْفَعُ دَرَجَةً عِنْدَ اللَّهِ؛ لِيَشْفَعَ في ولَدِهِ، وكَذا الوَلَدُ في والِدَيْهِ. وقالَ مُجاهِدٌ وابْنُ سِيرِينَ والسُّدِّيُّ: مَعْناهُ في الدُّنْيا، أيْ: إذا اضْطُرَّ إلى إنْفاقِهِمْ لِلْفاقَةِ. ونَحا إلَيْهِ الزَّجّاجُ، وقَدْ يُنْفِقُونَ دُونَ اضْطِرارٍ. وقالَ ابْنُ زَيْدٍ: في الدُّنْيا والآخِرَةِ، واللَّفْظُ يَقْتَضِي ذَلِكَ. ورُوِيَ عَنْ مُجاهِدٍ: أقْرَبُ لَكم نَفْعًا في المِيراثِ والشَّفاعَةِ. وقالَ ابْنُ بَحْرٍ: أسْرَعُ مَوْتًا فَيَرِثُهُ الآخَرُ. وقالَ ابْنُ عِيسى: أيْ فاقْسِمُوا المِيراثَ عَلى ما بَيَّنَ لَكم مَن يَعْلَمُ النَّفْعَ والمَصْلَحَةَ، فَإنَّكم لا تَدْرُونَ أنْتُمْ ذَلِكَ، وقَرِيبٌ مِنهُ قَوْلُ الزَّجّاجِ. قالَ: مَعْنى الكَلامِ أنَّهُ تَعالى قَدْ فَرَضَ الفَرائِضَ عَلى ما هو عِنْدَهُ حِكْمَةً، ولَوْ وكَلَ ذَلِكَ إلَيْكم لَمْ تَعْلَمُوا أيُّهم أنْفَعُ لَكم، فَتَضَعُونَ الأمْوالَ عَلى غَيْرِ حِكْمَةٍ، ولِهَذا أتْبَعَهُ بِقَوْلِهِ: ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ عَلِيمًا حَكِيمًا﴾ ﴿"Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise."﴾ أيْ عَلِيمٌ بِما يَصْلُحُ لِخَلْقِهِ، حَكِيمٌ فِيما فَرَضَ. قالَ ابْنُ عَطِيَّةَ: وهَذا تَعْرِيضٌ لِلْحِكْمَةِ في ذَلِكَ، وتَأْنِيسٌ لِلْعَرَبِ الَّذِينَ كانُوا يُوَرِّثُونَ عَلى غَيْرِ هَذِهِ [p-187] الصِّفَةِ.

It was also said: this sentence includes a prohibition against wishing for the death of the one whose estate is inherited.

It was also said: the meaning of ﴿Whichever of them is nearer to you in benefit﴾ is that the father is nearer in protection and upbringing, or that the children are nearer in obedience, service and compassion. Close to this is the statement of Abu Ya'la, who said: its meaning is that fathers and sons vary in benefit, so that it is not known which of them is nearer in benefit, because children benefit from their fathers in their youth, and fathers benefit from their children in their old age.

Al-Zamakhshari, linking this sentence to the bequest (wasiyyah), and that it came to encourage it and affirm it, said: "You do not know which of your fathers and your sons who die is more beneficial to you, whether the one who made a bequest among them or the one who did not make one. He means: whoever makes a bequest of part of his wealth, thereby exposing you to the reward of the Hereafter by carrying out his bequest, is nearer to you in benefit and more present in gain than one who leaves no bequest and so spares you worldly goods. He made the reward of the Hereafter nearer and more present than worldly goods, going to the reality of the matter, because worldly goods, although immediate and near in appearance, are perishable, so in reality they are the most distant and far off, whereas the reward of the Hereafter, although delayed, is lasting, so in reality it is the nearest and closest." End of his words. That is his speech.

The bequest is not mentioned in the verse for the sake of its legislation and rulings in themselves. Its mention came only to show that the division takes place after it is carried out and after the debt is settled, so it is not something that arises from it, and this sentence is explained by it. However, since the ruling on son and father in inheritance differs, the ruling was that if the father dies leaving a son and a daughter, the son inherits the share of two daughters; and the ruling for the two parents, if a son dies leaving them and a child, is that each of them inherits a sixth. It would come to mind that the father's share should be greater than the son's share, because of the kindness and upbringing the father gave the child from his youth to his acquiring of wealth until his death, together with what the son is commanded to do during his father's lifetime, namely to be dutiful to him. Or his share could be equal to his son's share in that situation, treating the root (the ascendant) like the branch (the descendant) in inheritance. God, exalted is He, made clear that this division is the division He chose and legislated, and that the fathers and sons for whose inheritance He legislated what He legislated, we do not know which of them is nearer in benefit. Rather, knowledge of that is entrusted to God's knowledge and wisdom. So what He legislated is the truth, not what occurs to our minds. When knowledge of that is hidden from us, we should not plunge into what we do not know, for these are arrangements from the Lawgiver whose causes we do not know or grasp. Rather, it is obligatory to submit to God and His Messenger regarding them. All legal determinations whose causes cannot be understood are alike in this, like the division of inheritances.

They said: ﴿أيُّهم﴾ (Ayyuhum, "which of them") is in the nominative as the subject (mubtada'), its predicate is ﴿أقْرَبُ﴾ (aqrabu, "nearer"), and the clause is in the accusative position as the object of ﴿تَدْرُونَ﴾ (tadrun, "you know"). ﴿تَدْرُونَ﴾ is one of the verbs of the heart (af'al al-qulub, verbs expressing mental states such as knowing and thinking). ﴿أيُّهم﴾ is an interrogative whose governing verb has been suspended from acting on its wording, because an interrogative, when not used to seek confirmation, is not governed by what precedes it, as established in the science of grammar. In my view there is another permissible possibility, which they did not mention, and it is according to the position of Sibawayh: that ﴿أيُّهم﴾ be a relative pronoun (mawsulah) built on the dhamma (vowel), and be the object of ﴿تَدْرُونَ﴾, and ﴿أقْرَبُ﴾ be the predicate of a deleted subject, its estimated form being: "they are nearer." This is like the statement of God, exalted is He: ﴿Then We will surely drag out from every party whichever of them is most obstinate﴾ [Maryam: 69]. The condition for its being built is met, namely that it is grammatically attached to a noun (mudafah lafzan), and the first part of its relative clause is omitted.

﴿فَرِيضَةً مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ (fariḍatan min Allah, "an obligation from God"): ﴿فَرِيضَةً﴾ is in the accusative as a verbal noun (masdar) emphasizing the meaning of the preceding sentence, because the meaning of ﴿يُوصِيكُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ (God enjoins you) is: God obligates for you. Makki and others said: it is an emphatic circumstantial accusative (hal), because the obligation (fariḍah) is not a verbal noun.

﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ عَلِيمًا حَكِيمًا﴾ [al-Nisa': 24]: that is, God is All-Knowing of the interests of His servants, All-Wise in what He ordained and divided of inheritances and other matters. The discussion of ﴿كانَ﴾ (kana, "was") has already been presented when it occurs to attribute a report to God, exalted is He. As for one who claims that it is the complete verb (tammah), with ﴿عَلِيمًا﴾ in the accusative as a circumstantial clause, his statement is weak; and as for one who claims that it is a superfluous particle (za'idah), his statement is erroneous.

Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 4, verse 12 (part 1 of 2):

﴿And for you is half of what your wives leave, if they have no child. But if they have a child, then for you is a quarter of what they leave, after any bequest they make or debt.﴾ When Allah the Exalted mentioned the inheritance of descendants from ascendants, and the inheritance of ascendants from descendants, He proceeded to mention the inheritance of those connected by a cause (sabab), not by lineage (nasab), and this is the case of marriage here. The Qur'an does not mention inheritance by reason of walaʾ (clientage). The inheritance that is established in the Sharia is by lineage and by the cause that encompasses marriage and walaʾ. In the early period of Islam, inheritance was by mutual alliance (muwalah), by adoption (khalaf) and by emigration (hijrah), and that was abrogated (nusikha dhalika). The inheritance by the cause of marriage is mentioned before the kalalah, even though the latter is by lineage, because of the close bond between the spouses, their connection, and the fact that each of them is independent of the other's companionship in a way that does not apply to kalalah relations. The address begins with men because of the degrees (darajat) that they have over women. Since a male child's share alongside a female is like the share of two females, in the case of marriage it is made: the male has the share of two females. The meaning of ﴿if they have a child﴾ is: from you, O heirs, or from others. Apparently "child" (walad) here refers to anyone whom she has borne in her womb, male or female, one or more; and the ruling for the sons of males from her, however far down they go, is the ruling of a child of the womb, in that the husband's fixed share from her is a quarter when a descendant exists, by consensus.

﴿And for them is a quarter of what you leave, if you have no child. But if you have a child, then for them is an eighth of what you leave, after any bequest you make or debt.﴾ The "child" here is like the child in that verse. The quarter and the eighth are shared by the wives if there are several, and one wife has it alone. The apparent meaning of the verse is that they are given their stated shares mentioned in the two verses without awl (increase of shares), and Ibn Abbas went to this view. The majority held that awl applies to the shares of husband and wife, as it applies to all the stated shares.

﴿And if a man leaves an inheritance by kalalah, or a woman, and he has a brother or a sister, then for each of the two is a sixth﴾ Kalalah is the absence of a father and a child from the deceased, so said Abu Bakr, Umar, Ali, Sulaym ibn Ubayd, al-Suddi, al-Hakam, Ibn Zayd and al-Sabiʿi. Another group said: it is only the absence of a child. It is narrated from Abu Bakr and Umar that they then reverted from it to the first view. It is also narrated from Ibn Abbas, and that is established from his statement about siblings alongside the parents: that they reduce the mother's share and take what they reduce. It follows from his view, if he inherited them, that the case of kalalah would give them a third by the text. Another group, including al-Hakam ibn Uyaynah, said: it is the absence of a child. Ibn Atiyyah said: these two views are weak, because whoever has a surviving father or child is inherited by lineage, not by kalalah. The community has now agreed that siblings do not inherit alongside a son or a father, and on this the eras and the lands have proceeded. End.

It has been disputed as to its derivation. It was said: from al-kalal, which is fatigue, as if the inheritance reaches the heir after weariness. Al-Aʿsha said:
"So I swore I would not weep for her from kalalah nor from weariness, until we meet Muhammad."
Al-Zamakhshari said: kalalah is originally a verbal noun meaning kalal, which is the departure of strength through fatigue. It was borrowed for kinship from a direction other than child or parent, because in relation to its relatives it is weak and frail. End. It was also said: it is derived from takallalahu al-nasab, meaning the lineage encircled him, surrounded him. When he leaves neither father nor child, his two sides are cut off, and these are the two pillars of his lineage, and his inheritance remains for those whom his lineage encircles, that is, surrounds him from its sides like a crown. From this comes "a garden crowned with blossoms." al-Farazdaq said:
"You inherited the spear of glory, not from kalalah, from the two sons of Manaf, Abd Shams and Hashim."
Al-Akhfash said: kalalah is one whom neither father nor mother inherits. What the majority holds is that kalalah is the deceased who has no child and no ascendant, and this is the view of the majority of linguists, the author of al-Ayn, Abu Mansur al-Lughawi, Ibn Arafah, Ibn al-Anbari, al-Utbi and Abu Ubaydah. Abu Ubaydah erred in mentioning the brother along with the father and child, and Qutrub erred in his statement that kalalah is the name for everyone other than the two parents and the brother; and what is other than father and child is called kalalah because, with the loss of its two sides, the heirs encircle it and go around it from its sides. This view is supported by the revelation of the verse concerning Jabir, who had no son or father on the day it was revealed, because his father had been killed at Uhud, so the story of Jabir became an explanation of the meaning of the verse. As for kalalah in the verse, Ata said: it is the wealth. Another group said: kalalah is the heirs, and this is the view of al-Raghib, who said: kalalah is a name for every heir. The poet said:
"The man gathers for wealth and for the kalalah what he herds."
Umar and Ibn Abbas said: kalalah is the deceased whose estate is inherited. Another group said: all the heirs together are kalalah.

al-Jumhur read ﴿yuwrathu﴾ with a fatha on the ra', in the passive voice, from awratha in the passive. al-Hasan read it with a kasra, in the active voice, from awratha also. Abu Rajaʾ, al-Hasan and al-Aʿmash read it with a kasra and shadda on the ra', from wa-rratha. As for the reading of the majority, and the meaning of kalalah being the deceased or the heir, the accusative of kalalah is a circumstantial accusative (hal) from the pronoun hidden in ﴿yuwrathu﴾. When it refers to the heir, one must assume "dhu kalalah" (one who has kalalah), because kalalah then is not the same as the pronoun in ﴿yuwrathu﴾. If the meaning of kalalah is kinship, its accusative is as an object of purpose (maf'ul li-ajlihi), meaning: he is inherited because of kalalah. As for the reading of al-Hasan and Abu Rajaʾ, if kalalah is the deceased, its accusative is circumstantial, and the two objects are omitted; the sense is: he bequeaths to his heir his wealth while being kalalah. If the intended meaning is the heir, the accusative of kalalah is the object of ﴿yuwrathu﴾, and the second object is omitted, its assumed form being: his wealth or the kinship is inherited as kalalah; the accusative as object of purpose and the two objects are both omitted as well. The verb kana may be incomplete (naqisah), so that ﴿yuwrathu﴾ is in the accusative position as predicate; or complete (tammah), so that it is in the nominative position as an adjective. If kana is incomplete and kalalah means the deceased, it is permissible for ﴿yuwrathu﴾ to be an adjective and ﴿kalalah﴾ accusative as the predicate of kana; or kalalah means the heir, and that is permissible by omitting an attributive noun, meaning: if there is a man inherited who is possessed of kalalah. Ata said: kalalah is the wealth, so ﴿kalalah﴾ is accusative as a second object, whether the verb is active or passive. Ibn Zayd said: kalalah is the inheritance, and it is accusative as a circumstantial or as an attribute of an omitted verbal noun, its assumed form being: an inheritance of kalalah.

* *

The disagreement over kalalah has been extensive, and the summary of what has been said about it is: that it is the heir, or the deceased inherited, or the inherited wealth, or the inheritance, or the kinship. The apparent meaning of ﴿yuwrathu﴾ is: it is inherited from him, so that he is the one inherited, not the heir. The reading of those who read the ra' with kasra clarifies this. Al-Zamakhshari said: If you ask, if you make yuwrathu passive from awratha, what is its sense? I say: the man then is the heir, not the one inherited. If you ask, to whom does the pronoun in ﴿fa-li-kulli wahidin minhuma﴾ refer then? I say: to the man and to his brother and sister; and on the first reading, to the two of them. If you ask, when the pronoun refers to the two of them, does it convey equality of the two in taking the sixth without preference of male over female, and does this benefit remain in this sense? I say: yes; because when you say, the sixth is for him, or for one of the brother or sister by choice, you have equated male and female. End of his words. The summary of what he said: the meaning is: if one of the two whom he inherits, other than them, a man or woman, has one of these two, a brother or sister, then for each of them is a sixth. He conjoined woman to man and omitted from it what restricts the man, by the indication of meaning, the sense being: or a woman who is inherited by kalalah. Though mere conjunction does not require restricting the conjoined by the restriction of the conjoined-to. The pronoun in ﴿wa-lahu﴾ refers back to the man, like ﴿wa-idha ra'aw tijaratan aw lahwan infaddu ilayha﴾ [al-Jumuʿah: 11] in that it refers back to the first term conjoined. Though it is permissible to refer the pronoun back to the conjoined term; you say: Zayd or Hind stood, as al-Akhfash and al-Farra' relate. The mention of this ruling has already preceded for us. Al-Farra' added a third way, which is that the pronoun is attributed to both of them. Al-Farra' said: the custom of the Arabs, when they put alternation between two nouns with "aw", is to refer the pronoun to both of them together, or to one of them, whichever you choose. You say: whoever has a brother or a sister, let him maintain relations with him; or if you wish, let him maintain relations with her. End. On this view, the apparent meaning is His words: ﴿If he is rich or poor, Allah is more entitled to both of them﴾ [al-Nisa': 135], and those who forbade this way have interpreted it.

The root of ukht is akhawah on the pattern of sharrah, just as bint originally is banayah according to one of the two opinions concerning ibn, whether the omitted element is a waw or a ya'. It was said: when the final radical and the feminine ta' were omitted, and they assimilated the word to qufl and jidh by adding a ta' at the end of both, al-Farra' said: the first letter of ukht is given a damma to indicate that the omitted element is a waw, and the first letter of bint is given a kasra to indicate that the omitted element is a ya'. End. This ta' of attachment indicates what the feminine ta' indicates of femininity. The apparent meaning of His words ﴿wa-lahu akhun aw ukht﴾ is unrestricted, since brotherhood applies to full siblings, to consanguine siblings and to half-siblings from different fathers; and they agreed that what is meant in this verse is uterine siblings. The reading of Ubayy clarifies this: ﴿wa-lahu akhun aw ukhtun min al-umm﴾ (and he has a brother or a sister from the mother), and the reading of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas: ﴿wa-lahu akhun aw ukhtun min ummin﴾. The difference between the two rulings here and at the end of the surah indicates a difference in the one ruled for: for here the sons or siblings share only the third, males or females equally among them. There, they take the whole estate, with the male receiving the equivalent of the share of two females, and the two daughters receive two-thirds. The pronoun in ﴿minhuma﴾ apparently refers to ﴿akhun aw ukht﴾. On what al-Zamakhshari permitted, it refers to one of the man or woman and one of the brother or sister. If a man dies leaving a husband, a mother and full siblings, then the husband has a half, the mother and the uterine siblings a sixth, and the remainder goes to the full siblings; or two uterine brothers with full brothers, this is the Himadiyyah case. Do all share in the third, or do the two uterine brothers alone take it? There are two opinions: Umar at the end of his judgments, Ibn Mas'ud, Zayd ibn Thabit, Abu Hanifah and his companions held for sharing; and Ali, Abu Musa, Ubayy and Ibn Abbas held for the separate share.

﴿But if they are more than that, they are partners in the third﴾ The demonstrative "that" refers to a brother or a sister, that is, more than one. Because the one ruled to have the sixth is each of the brother and the sister individually, so it is one; and the ruling was not made that the two together have the sixth, so the plurality is valid for what is pointed to, which is "that". Rather the meaning here by "more than" is: if the one who inherits is in excess of that, that is, more than the single one; because it is not valid to say "this is more than one" except with this meaning, since the meanings of "many" and "one" are contradictory, as there is no plurality in one. In His words ﴿if they are﴾ and ﴿then they are partners﴾ the masculine pronoun predominates, and for this reason it comes with waw and with the word fa-hum; all this is according to how the rulings have been established. The apparent meaning of the verse is: if he leaves one brother or sister, that is, one of these two, then each of them has a sixth; or more, they share in the third. As for if he leaves two of a brother or sister, the apparent meaning of the verse does not indicate that.

Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 4, verse 12 (part 2 of 2):

﴿After a bequest he makes or a debt, without causing harm: an ordinance from Allah﴾. The pronoun in ﴿yūṣā﴾ (is bequeathed) refers back to "a man" (rajul), just as it refers back to him in ﴿and he has a brother﴾. What strengthens the return of the pronoun to him is that he is the one who dies leaving the estate (al-mawrūth), not the heir (al-wārith), for it is the one who makes the bequest, or on whom the debt lies, who is the deceased (al-mawrūth), not the heir. As for whoever interprets His saying ﴿and if a man [has no descendants]﴾ as meaning the heir and not the deceased, he makes the subject of ﴿yūṣā﴾ refer to what the meaning indicates of the heir, just as the meaning indicates the subject in His saying ﴿then for them is two-thirds of what he left﴾ [al-Nisa: 11], because it is known that the one who bequeaths and leaves behind is none other than the deceased, not the heir.

The meaning is: without causing harm to his heirs through his bequest or his debt. The forms of harm are many: such as bequeathing more than a third, or bequeathing to an heir, or bequeathing a third while selling something to someone at less than its value, or gifting it, or devoting it to acts of piety such as manumission and the like, fleeing from a needy heir, or acknowledging a debt that he does not owe. The well-known position of the school of Malik is that as long as it remains within a third, it is not considered harmful. It is appropriate to take into account this condition, namely the absence of harm, in what precedes in His saying ﴿after a bequest he makes﴾ (and "you bequeath" and "they bequeath" [in the feminine] is an elision from what came before, indicating what follows it), so the absence of harm is not restricted in meaning to this later verse.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: "Harm in a bequest is among the major sins," and he narrated it from the Prophet (ﷺ). And from him (ﷺ), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah: "Whoever causes harm in his bequest, Allah will cast him into the valley of Hell." Al-Suddi said: "Allah forbade harm during life and at death."

They said: the accusative of ﴿without causing harm﴾ is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) from the concealed pronoun in ﴿yūṣā﴾, and the governing element for both is ﴿yūṣā﴾. But what they said is not permissible, because it involves separating the governor and the governed by a foreign element from both, namely His saying ﴿or a debt﴾; for "or a debt" is conjoined to "a bequest" which is qualified by the governor of the circumstantial clause. Had it been as they said regarding the grammar, the construction would have been: ﴿after a bequest he is bequeathed, without causing harm, or a debt﴾. And according to the reading of whoever reads ﴿yūṣā﴾ with a fatḥah on the ṣād in the passive voice, it cannot be a circumstantial clause for the reason we mentioned, and also because the one causing harm is not mentioned, since it is elided and replaced by the unnamed passive subject (nāʾib al-fāʿil), and it is not valid for a circumstantial clause to occur from that elided element. If you say "the winds are sent (tursalu al-riyāḥ) bringing good news (mubashshiran bihā)" with a kasrah on the shīn, it is not permissible, even though the meaning is "Allah sends the winds bringing good news with them." What appears is that a governing element is to be supposed for it, indicated by the meaning preceding it, and it is general in meaning with respect to what exercises control over the property through the bequest or the debt; its estimate is: "that binds his property or obligates it upon him, without causing harm to his heirs by that binding or obligating." It has also been said: ﴿yūṣī﴾ [al-Nisa: 11] is supposed as the governor, because of the indication of ﴿yūṣā﴾ upon it, like the reading ﴿yusabbaḥu﴾ with a fatḥah on the bāʾ. And some men said: i.e., men glorify Him (yusabbiḥuhu rijāl).

The accusative of ﴿an ordinance from Allah﴾ is as an emphatic verbal noun (maṣdar mu'akkid), meaning: Allah enjoins you concerning that as an enjoining (yūṣīkumu Allāhu bi-dhālika waṣiyyatan), just as ﴿an obligation from Allah﴾ [al-Nisa: 11] is accusative.

Ibn ʿAtiyyah said: it is a verbal noun in the position of a circumstantial clause, the governor being ﴿yūṣīkum﴾ [al-Nisa: 11]. It has also been said: it is accusative by way of departure from His saying ﴿then for each one of them is a sixth﴾, or from His saying ﴿then they are partners in the third﴾. He and al-Zamakhshari permitted the accusative of "an ordinance" by ﴿without causing harm﴾ in a figurative sense, because the harm in reality occurs to the heirs, not to the bequest; but since the heirs are those for whom Allah the Exalted has enjoined the bequest, the harm inflicted upon the heirs is as if it had been inflicted upon the bequest. This interpretation is supported by the reading of al-Hasan: "ghayra muḍārri waṣiyyatin" with a kasrah on the tanwīn, so that "waṣiyyatan" is in the genitive by the attachment of ﴿muḍārr﴾ to it. It is like "yā sāriqa al-laylah" (O thief of the night); the meaning is "O my thieves in the night," but the verb was extended, transferring it to the adverbial complement as it would be transferred to the direct object. Likewise the estimate here is: "without causing harm in an ordinance from Allah," so the active participle was extended and transferred to what reaches it through an intermediary, as in its transitivity to the direct object.

﴿And Allah is All-Knowing, Most Forbearing﴾. All-Knowing of whoever oppresses or acts justly; Most Forbearing toward the oppressor, not hastening to punish him, so said al-Zamakhshari. In it is the subtle trace of Muʿtazilism, that is, that the oppressor, even if Allah does not hasten to punish him, must nonetheless receive it. What the word ḥalīm indicates is that He does not take to account for the sin, as the people of the Sunnah say. And according to their view, this attribute indicates pardon of it altogether. This is fitting here, because when He described Himself by saying "All-Knowing," and indicated His awareness of what the deceased does in harming his heirs through his bequest and debt, and that the mention of His knowledge of that is evidence of recompense for that harm, He followed it with the attribute that indicates forgiveness toward whomever He wills. This is in the manner of most of the Qur'an: it does not mention what indicates punishment without following it with what indicates pardon. And observe the excellence of this division in inheritance: the cause of inheritance is connection to the deceased; if it is without an intermediary, it is either lineage (nasab) or marriage (zawjiyyah); or with an intermediary, it is kalalah. The first is placed before the second because it is intrinsic (dhātī), and the second is accidental (ʿaraḍ). And kalalah is delayed after them because the two (lineage and marriage) cannot be subject to complete removal, and because their connection is without intermediary, and because of the greater frequency of association. Ends, summarized from the words of al-Razi in his tafsir.

﴿Those are the limits of Allah﴾. It has been said that the reference of "those" (تِلْكَ) is to the division of inheritance mentioned earlier. The more appropriate view is that it refers to the rulings mentioned previously concerning orphans, wives, bequests and inheritance. These laws are called limits (ḥudūd) because they are prescribed for the responsible persons, who may not transgress them to something else. Ibn 'Abbas said: the limits of Allah are obedience to Him. al-Suddi said: they are His conditions. It has been said: they are His obligations. It has also been said: they are His sunan (established practices). These statements are close in meaning. (p-192)

﴿And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, He will admit him into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. That is the great triumph﴾. When Allah, may He be exalted, referred to the limits He had set, He divided people into one who acts upon them in obedience and one who does not act upon them and is disobedient. He began with the obedient, because obedience is the predominant characteristic of one who is a believer in Allah, may He be exalted, since the surah opens by addressing people in general, and then continues with address to those who have faith, up to the end of the inheritance rulings. Also, the part concerning good should be begun with and given priority. The pronoun was first treated according to the wording of man (مَن) in His saying يُطِعِ and يُدْخِلْهُ, so it was singular. Then it was treated according to the meaning in His saying خالِدِينَ. The accusative of خالِدِينَ is a ḥāl (circumstantial accusative, describing the state of the subject at the time of the action), governed by يُدْخِلْهُ, and its ṣāḥib al-ḥāl (the word it describes) is the object pronoun in يُدْخِلْهُ. Ibn 'Atiyya said: "He put خالِدِينَ in the plural according to the meaning of مَن after the singular had come first, out of regard for the wording of مَن, and the reverse of this is not permitted." End of quote. What he mentioned, that it is not permitted to move from treating it according to meaning and then according to wording, is permitted according to the grammarians. The details and the disagreement regarding observing both treatments are mentioned in the lengthy books of grammar. al-Zamakhshari said: "خالِدِينَ and خالِدًا are in the accusative as ḥāl. If you ask: may they be two adjectives of جَنّاتٍ and نارًا? I say: No, because they refer to something other than the one they belong to, so there must be a pronoun, which is your saying: خالِدِينَ هم فِيها (abiding therein, they), and خالِدًا هو فِيها (abiding therein, he)." End of quote. What he mentioned is not agreed upon; rather it is a ruling based on the school of the al-Basriyyun (the Basran grammarians). As for the al-Kufiyyun (the Kufan grammarians), it is permitted, and the pronoun need not be made explicit, provided there is no ambiguity; there is a detailed discussion of this in the grammar books. al-Zajjaj permitted this in the verse, and al-Tibrizi followed the view of the al-Kufiyyun. Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir read نُدْخِلْهُ here and in نُدْخِلْهُ نارًا with the plural of majesty (نون العظمة). The rest read it with yā' (يُدْخِلْهُ), referring to Allah, may He be exalted. al-Raghib said: The describing of the triumph as "great" is in consideration of the triumph of this world, which is described in His saying: ﴿Say: The enjoyment of this world is little﴾ [al-Nisa': 77], and the small and the little are close in describing both.

﴿And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger and transgresses His limits, He will admit him into the Fire, abiding therein forever, and for him is a humiliating punishment﴾. When He mentioned the reward of the one who observes the limits, He mentioned the punishment of the one who transgresses them, and He made the matter of sins severe. He did not suffice with disobedience but emphasized it by His saying: ﴿and transgresses His limits﴾. The ending with the humiliating punishment is appropriate, because the disobedient one who transgresses the limits appears in the form of one who is deceived and emboldened against the disobedience of Allah. The concern for hardships may diminish as long as humiliation is not joined to them, and for this reason they said: "Death, but not disgrace." It has been said: He used the singular khālidan (خالدًا) here and the plural khālidīna fīhā (خالِدِينَ فِيها) elsewhere, because the people of obedience are the people of intercession; when one intercedes for others, they enter it (Paradise), whereas the disobedient one does not enter the Fire with someone else, so he remains alone. End of quote. These verses include types of rhetorical beauty (badī'): the detailing of the heirs and the shares after the generality in His saying: ﴿For men there is a share﴾ [al-Nisa': 7], and the shift from the form "Allah commands you" (يَأْمُرُكُمُ اللَّهُ) to ﴿He instructs you﴾ [al-Nisa': 11], because of the emphasis and the eagerness to follow that which is in a bequest. Also antithesis (ṭibāq) in ﴿the male's share equals the share of two females﴾ [al-Nisa': 11], and in مَن يُطِعْ and مَن يَعْصِ; the return of the pronoun to something not mentioned, for the strength of indication in His saying مِمّا تَرَكَ, meaning: what the deceased left. Also repetition in the word (كانَ), in ﴿an obligation from Allah﴾ [al-Nisa': 11], إنَّ اللَّهَ, in ولَدًا and أبَواهُ, in ﴿after any bequest he has made or debt﴾ [al-Nisa': 12], in ﴿an ordinance from Allah﴾ [al-Nisa': 12] إنَّ اللَّهَ, in ﴿the limits of Allah﴾, and in ﴿Allah and His Messenger﴾. Also the turning of address in the reading of the one who reads نُدْخِلْهُ with the nūn, and omission in several places.

﴿Those are the limits of Allah﴾. It has been said that the reference of "those" (تِلْكَ) is to the division of inheritance mentioned earlier. The more appropriate view is that it refers to the rulings mentioned previously concerning orphans, wives, bequests and inheritance. These laws are called limits (ḥudūd) because they are prescribed for the responsible persons, who may not transgress them to something else. Ibn 'Abbas said: the limits of Allah are obedience to Him. al-Suddi said: they are His conditions. It has been said: they are His obligations. It has also been said: they are His sunan (established practices). These statements are close in meaning. (p-192)

﴿And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, He will admit him into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. That is the great triumph﴾. When Allah, may He be exalted, referred to the limits He had set, He divided people into one who acts upon them in obedience and one who does not act upon them and is disobedient. He began with the obedient, because obedience is the predominant characteristic of one who is a believer in Allah, may He be exalted, since the surah opens by addressing people in general, and then continues with address to those who have faith, up to the end of the inheritance rulings. Also, the part concerning good should be begun with and given priority. The pronoun was first treated according to the wording of man (مَن) in His saying يُطِعِ and يُدْخِلْهُ, so it was singular. Then it was treated according to the meaning in His saying خالِدِينَ. The accusative of خالِدِينَ is a ḥāl (circumstantial accusative, describing the state of the subject at the time of the action), governed by يُدْخِلْهُ, and its ṣāḥib al-ḥāl (the word it describes) is the object pronoun in يُدْخِلْهُ. Ibn 'Atiyya said: "He put خالِدِينَ in the plural according to the meaning of مَن after the singular had come first, out of regard for the wording of مَن, and the reverse of this is not permitted." End of quote. What he mentioned, that it is not permitted to move from treating it according to meaning and then according to wording, is permitted according to the grammarians. The details and the disagreement regarding observing both treatments are mentioned in the lengthy books of grammar. al-Zamakhshari said: "خالِدِينَ and خالِدًا are in the accusative as ḥāl. If you ask: may they be two adjectives of جَنّاتٍ and نارًا? I say: No, because they refer to something other than the one they belong to, so there must be a pronoun, which is your saying: خالِدِينَ هم فِيها (abiding therein, they), and خالِدًا هو فِيها (abiding therein, he)." End of quote. What he mentioned is not agreed upon; rather it is a ruling based on the school of the al-Basriyyun (the Basran grammarians). As for the al-Kufiyyun (the Kufan grammarians), it is permitted, and the pronoun need not be made explicit, provided there is no ambiguity; there is a detailed discussion of this in the grammar books. al-Zajjaj permitted this in the verse, and al-Tibrizi followed the view of the al-Kufiyyun. Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir read نُدْخِلْهُ here and in نُدْخِلْهُ نارًا with the plural of majesty (نون العظمة). The rest read it with yā' (يُدْخِلْهُ), referring to Allah, may He be exalted. al-Raghib said: The describing of the triumph as "great" is in consideration of the triumph of this world, which is described in His saying: ﴿Say: The enjoyment of this world is little﴾ [al-Nisa': 77], and the small and the little are close in describing both.

﴿And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger and transgresses His limits, He will admit him into the Fire, abiding therein forever, and for him is a humiliating punishment﴾. When He mentioned the reward of the one who observes the limits, He mentioned the punishment of the one who transgresses them, and He made the matter of sins severe. He did not suffice with disobedience but emphasized it by His saying: ﴿and transgresses His limits﴾. The ending with the humiliating punishment is appropriate, because the disobedient one who transgresses the limits appears in the form of one who is deceived and emboldened against the disobedience of Allah. The concern for hardships may diminish as long as humiliation is not joined to them, and for this reason they said: "Death, but not disgrace." It has been said: He used the singular khālidan (خالدًا) here and the plural khālidīna fīhā (خالِدِينَ فِيها) elsewhere, because the people of obedience are the people of intercession; when one intercedes for others, they enter it (Paradise), whereas the disobedient one does not enter the Fire with someone else, so he remains alone. End of quote. These verses include types of rhetorical beauty (badī'): the detailing of the heirs and the shares after the generality in His saying: ﴿For men there is a share﴾ [al-Nisa': 7], and the shift from the form "Allah commands you" (يَأْمُرُكُمُ اللَّهُ) to ﴿He instructs you﴾ [al-Nisa': 11], because of the emphasis and the eagerness to follow that which is in a bequest. Also antithesis (ṭibāq) in ﴿the male's share equals the share of two females﴾ [al-Nisa': 11], and in مَن يُطِعْ and مَن يَعْصِ; the return of the pronoun to something not mentioned, for the strength of indication in His saying مِمّا تَرَكَ, meaning: what the deceased left. Also repetition in the word (كانَ), in ﴿an obligation from Allah﴾ [al-Nisa': 11], إنَّ اللَّهَ, in ولَدًا and أبَواهُ, in ﴿after any bequest he has made or debt﴾ [al-Nisa': 12], in ﴿an ordinance from Allah﴾ [al-Nisa': 12] إنَّ اللَّهَ, in ﴿the limits of Allah﴾, and in ﴿Allah and His Messenger﴾. Also the turning of address in the reading of the one who reads نُدْخِلْهُ with the nūn, and omission in several places.

(p-193) ﴿And those of your women who commit lewdness, bring against them four witnesses from among you. If they testify, then confine them to their houses until death takes them or Allah ordains for them a way.﴾ ﴿And the two of you who commit it, harm them. If they repent and amend, then leave them alone. Indeed, Allah is ever Accepting of repentance, Merciful.﴾ ﴿Repentance is only incumbent upon Allah for those who do evil in ignorance and then repent soon. Those are the ones whose repentance Allah accepts, and Allah is ever Knowing, Wise.﴾ [al-Nisa': 17] ﴿Repentance is not for those who do evil deeds until, when death approaches one of them, he says, "Indeed I have repented now," nor for those who die while they are disbelievers. For those We have prepared a painful punishment.﴾ [al-Nisa': 18] ﴿O you who believe, it is not lawful for you to inherit women by force, nor to restrain them in order to take back part of what you have given them, unless they commit a clear immorality. And live with them in kindness. If you dislike them, perhaps you dislike something in which Allah has placed much good.﴾ [al-Nisa': 19] ﴿And if you wish to replace one wife with another, and you have given one of them a heap of gold, do not take back anything from it. Would you take it by slander and manifest sin?﴾ [al-Nisa': 20] ﴿And how could you take it, when you have been intimate with one another and they have taken from you a solemn covenant?﴾ [al-Nisa': 21] ﴿And do not marry those whom your fathers married, except what has already passed. Indeed, it was an immorality and hatred and an evil way.﴾ [al-Nisa': 22] ﴿Forbidden to you are your mothers, your daughters, your sisters, your paternal aunts, your maternal aunts, your brothers' daughters, your sisters' daughters, your foster mothers, your foster sisters, your wives' mothers, your stepdaughters in your guardianship born of the wives with whom you have consummated marriage (but if you have not consummated, there is no blame on you), the wives of your sons who are from your loins, and combining two sisters, except what has already passed. Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving, Merciful.﴾ [al-Nisa': 23] ﴿And [also forbidden are] married women, except those whom your right hands possess. This is the decree of Allah upon you. Lawful for you is what is beyond that, that you seek with your wealth, chaste and not fornicating. So whatever you enjoy from them, give them their due compensation as an obligation. And there is no blame upon you for what you mutually agree after the obligation. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing, Wise.﴾ [al-Nisa': 24] ﴿And whoever among you cannot afford to marry free believing women, then [he may marry] from what your right hands possess of your believing young women. And Allah is most knowing of your faith; you are of one another. So marry them with the permission of their families and give them their compensation in kindness, [they being] chaste, not fornicating and not taking secret lovers. And when they are married and then commit immorality, their punishment is half that of free women. That is for one of you who fears hardship; but to be patient is better for you. And Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.﴾ [al-Nisa': 25] ﴿Allah wants to make clear to you and to guide you to the ways of those before you and to turn to you in forgiveness. And Allah is Knowing, Wise.﴾ [al-Nisa': 26] ﴿And Allah wants to turn to you in forgiveness, while those who follow their desires want you to deviate into a great deviation.﴾ [al-Nisa': 27] ﴿Allah wants to lighten [the burden] for you, and man was created weak.﴾ [al-Nisa': 28]

Al-ʿIshrah (ʿishrah, companionship and association): al-ṣuḥbah and al-mukhālaṭah (close association and mixing). It is said: ʿāsharū, taʿāsharū, and iʿtasharū (they associated with one another). That [word] derives from ʿashr al-judhūr (the division of the palm-stumps into shares), because it involves division and mixing.

Al-ifḍāʾ ilā al-shayʾ (al-ifḍāʾ, reaching something): arriving at a fiḍāʾ (open expanse) of it, that is, a wide, unbounded space. In the proverb "al-nās fawḍā fuḍḍiya," meaning the people are mixed together, each touching the other. It is said: faḍā yafḍū faḍāʾan, when it became wide; the alif of afḍā is converted from a yā' whose root is wāw.

Al-maqt (maqt, detestation): hatred combined with contempt, arising from a shameful act committed by its doer.

Al-ʿammah (paternal aunt): the father's sister. Al-khālah (maternal aunt): the mother's sister, and its alif is converted from a wāw; the evidence is their saying akhwāl in the plural of khāl, and rajul mukhwil, meaning a man with noble maternal uncles.

Al-rabībah (stepdaughter): the daughter of a man's wife from another husband.

Al-ḥijr (ḥijr, with the ḥāʾ either fatḥah or kasrah): the front of a person's garment and what lies before him of it while wearing it. The word was then used for guarding and keeping, because the one who wears it protects a child and similar things in that part of the garment. Its plural is ḥujūr.

Al-ḥalīlah (ḥalīlah, wife) and al-ḥalīl (husband). The poet said:
"I visit the young woman of the tribe in the presence of her husband,
but when he goes out to raid with the army, I do not visit her."
She is called ḥalīlah because she alights (taḥull) with the husband wherever he alights, so it is faʿīlah in the sense of fāʿilah. Al-Zajjāj and others held that it derives from the word ḥalāl (lawful), so she is ḥalīlah in the sense of muḥallalah (made lawful). It is also said that each of them unties the other's waistwrap.

Al-ṣulb (ṣulb, the back): the spine. Ṣalaba ṣalābah means he became strong and firm. Al-Farrāʾ mentions in his book Lughāt al-Qurʾān that al-ṣulb, the back, is on the pattern of qufl, and that this is the dialect of the people of the Ḥijāz, while the Tamīm and Asad say al-ṣalab, with fatḥah on the ṣād and lām. He said: Someone recited to me:
"And a back like the supple, greased rein."
He said: Someone from Banū Asad recited to me:
"When I stand up, I complain about my back."

Al-muḥṣanah: a chaste woman. It is said: uḥṣinat, so she is muḥṣan, and ḥaṣunat, so she is ḥaṣān, meaning she refrained from suspicion and guarded herself against it. Shamir said: It is said, "a woman ḥaṣān and ḥāṣin." He said:
"And a guarded one, one of the guarded women, smooth, [protected] from harm and from separation from the Waqs."
The verbal noun of ḥaṣunat is ḥaṣn. Sibawayh said: Abū ʿUbaydah and al-Kisāʾī said: ḥaṣānah. It is said that the active participle of aḥṣana, asḥaba, and abʿaja is muftaʿil with a fatḥah on the middle radical; this is an anomaly transmitted by Thaʿlab from Ibn al-Aʿrābī. The root meaning of iḥṣān is prevention, and from it comes the word ḥaṣīnah for armour and for a city, and ḥiṣn (fortress), and "a horse ḥaṣān" (a chaste or well-protected horse).

Al-musāfaḥah and al-sifāḥ: fornication. Its root is from al-safḥ, which is pouring, because each of the two fornicators pours out his drop (nuṭfah).

Al-khidn and al-khadīn: the companion.

Al-ṭawl: superiority. It is said of it: ṭāla ʿalayhi yaṭūlu ṭawlan, meaning he surpassed him. Al-Layth and al-Zajjāj said: al-ṭawl is capability. End of quote. It is also said: ʿalayhi ṭawl, meaning an excess and superiority, and ṭālahu ṭawlan, so he is ṭāʾil. The poet said:
"Hatred of myself has increased for me, for I am
detested by every man who is not superior."
From it comes ṭūl in the body, because it is an addition to it, just as qiṣar (shortness) is a deficiency and shortfall in it.

Al-fatāh: a young person in the prime of youth; al-fatāʾ is youthfulness. He said: "Then chivalry and youthfulness have gone." Ibn Manṣūr al-Jawāliqī said: al-mutafattiyah and al-fatāh is the adolescent girl; al-fatā is the companion, and from it [comes the Qurʾanic phrase]: ﴿And when Moses said to his fatā﴾ [al-Kahf: 60]. Al-fatā also means the slave. From it [comes the Prophetic statement]: "None of you should say 'my slave' or 'my female slave,' but let him say 'my fatā' and 'my fatāt'."

Al-maylu: deviation from the path of straightness.

﴿And those of your women who commit lewdness, bring against them four witnesses from among you﴾. Mujāhid said, and Abū Muslim ibn Baḥr al-Iṣfahānī chose this view: this verse was revealed concerning women. The lewdness here means musāḥaqah (lesbianism), and their punishment was made confinement until they die or marry.
